:JUDGMENT:

: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH 5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 24.11.2021 at about 8.30 p.m. she had been travelling as passenger in auto bearing Reg.No. KA05AA562 which was driven by her husband on TuomkurBangalore NH48 Road, near Gundenahalli Village, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru, a Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN29BH2228 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against back side of the said auto, due to the impact she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Nelamangala Government Hospital, thereafter shifted to NIMHANS Hospital Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as indoor patient, for which she has spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
3. At the time of the accident she was aged about 45 years, hale and healthy, she is doing tailoring work, SCCH 5 thereby earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.
due to this accident she has lost income and earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.432/2021 is registered against the driver of the said lorry for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, he is not a proper and necessary party in the said case, as the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN29BH2228 has not at all involved in the SCCH 5 alleged accident, claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Further complaint is filed belatedly with the collusion of police, got implicated the lorry for their wrongful gain.
Further his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
There is no compliance of 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:

sentences.text: Whether Petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 24.11.2021 at about 8.30 p.m. when petitioner was proceeding as traveller of passenger auto bearing Reg.No.KA05AA562 the said auto was driving by his husband near TumkurBengalukru NH48 Road, near Gundenahalli Village, Nelamangala SCCH 5 Taluk, at that time, one Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN29 BH2228 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove her case, Petitioner herself deposed her evidence as PW1, examined one witness as PW2 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, counsel for R2 submitted that, he has no defence evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative SCCH 5 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:

::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:
In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW1, in her chiefexamination she has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.5,
copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8 and copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.11.
SCCH 5 9.
R1/owner has not contested the petition, R12/insure has contested the petition, but not disputed the place, date and time of the accident either in written statement or in crossexamination.
Further taken contention that, very lorry bearing Reg.No.TN29BH 2228 has not caused this accident.

Further taken contention that, auto driver had no driving licence and insurance, due to his own mistake auto is turtled down, so that, in order to protect the interest of the auto driver, false complaint is lodged against this lorry and its driver, but such suggestion is denied by this petitioner.
Rabiya Khanum vs Kaveri.K on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57585328/
3 10.
Insupport of her case, GDMO, NIMHANS Hospital Bengaluru is examined as PW2 and furnished trauma case sheet marked as Ex.P.13.
In cross examination also deposed that, petitioner has taken SCCH 5 treatment in their hospital out of this accident, some stitches were put on back side of the head.

11. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence, police papers speaks that, in middle of the road lorry came and dashed against the auto, said fact is clear from hand sketch map and charge sheet,
IMV report speaks that, front portion of both the vehicles are damaged.
Further police papers speaks lorry has dashed against the auto on its hind portion so that, petitioner has sustained injuries.
Considering the same, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the lorry driver.
It is defence of the R2 that, auto driver had no driving licence and insurance.

R1 has not at all contested the petition and not produced the said documents, only on the basis of non producing such documents, it is not possible to SCCH 5 presume that it is mistake of the auto driver.
Considering the same petitioner has proved above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:

As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 45 years, for proof of her age,
she has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.11, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.12.1977 and the alleged accident is occurred on 24.11.2021, accordingly relying on Ex.P.11, her age is considered about 44 years as on the date of accident.

As per her case,
she is doing tailoring work, thereby earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.
In this regard she has not produced any income proof documents.

13. As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained lacerated wound over back of the head,
which SCCH 5 is simple in nature.
In this regard she has produced copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7 issued by General Hospital Nelamangala.

Further she has produced outpatient record marked as Ex.P.9 medical bills of Rs.200/ marked as Ex.P.10.
14.
Further petitioner has not examined the Doctor regarding the nature of the injuries sustained by her in the accident.
Further in crossexamination petitioner admitted that, she has sustained only simple injuries, charge sheet is for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
As oer the wound certificate there are two injuries.
There is no opinion of the Doctor to say that, said injuries are grievous in nature.

So that, ignoring the charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sec.338 of IPC, considering the admission given by PW1 and wound certificate with SCCH 5 regard to simple injury, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, she has sustained only simple injuries but not grievous injuries.

Furthermore there is no evidence of the Doctor, no discharge summary and no disability certificate so that, petitioner is entitled for only global compensation of Rs.25,000/ along with medial bill of Rs.200/.
15.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.25,200/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

16. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.1710013120P111112394 which is valid for the period from 31.12.2020 to 30.12.2021, the alleged Rabiya Khanum vs Kaveri.K on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57585328/
4 accident was occurred on 24.11.2021 it reveals that, as on the date of SCCH 5 accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further driver of the offending lorry by name K.Periyannan had valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.25,200/
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Two Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH 5 The Respondent No..2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through epayment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
